approachQuestion.prompt:
Group exact payload copies

Input: an array payloads of byte strings. Return groups of original indices that have exactly equal byte sequences, including singleton groups. Order of groups and indices is arbitrary. Bytes can have any value from 0 to 255, and empty payloads are valid.

Example 1: payloads = [[0,255],[0,255],[255,0],[]]. Output: [[0,1],[2],[3]] in any order. Example 2: payloads = [[],[]]. Output: [[0,1]]. 0 ≤ n ≤ 100,000; total byte count B ≤ 1,000,000. A hash or digest collision is possible and must never merge unequal payloads. For complexity, assume a non-adversarial byte-string dictionary lookup/insertion for payload s has expected cost proportional to |s|+1, including hashing and exact equality checks; this is not a collision-free correctness assumption.

Constraints: input is immutable; all identifiers and numeric entries are signed 32-bit integers unless specified. Arithmetic uses signed 64-bit integers. Prefer the least expected running-time growth, then avoid unnecessary asymptotic auxiliary storage. Non-adversarial hashing of fixed-size integer keys/tuples has expected amortized constant cost.

options.text: Use a dictionary keyed by byte strings with exact byte-by-byte equality on hash collisions. Store a reference to the first input payload for each key and append indices to its bucket.
options.feedback: Hashes choose lookup candidates; exact equality decides membership. References to immutable input payloads avoid copying their contents.

options.text: Use the same exact-equality dictionary but copy every distinct key’s full bytes into separate owned storage before retaining it.
options.feedback: This is correct, but immutable input permits retained references, avoiding a byte-sized auxiliary copy that can dominate the number of payloads.

options.text: Group solely by a fixed-width digest and treat equal digests as proof of equal payloads.
options.feedback: The domain permits digest collisions. Two unequal payloads with the same digest would be merged, violating exact equality.
Payloads [0,255] and [255,0] have equal lengths but are different byte sequences.

feedback.reason: Distinguish a hash used for lookup from an exact key equality test required for correctness.
details: Use the stated exact-equality byte-string dictionary. Retain references to immutable input payloads as keys, without copying bytes. Append every original index to its bucket. Retain bucket lists and copy them into returned groups after all input is processed.

A hash narrows lookup candidates; exact byte equality determines grouping. Equal lengths or equal digests alone cannot prove identical payloads. Immutable input permits storing references rather than copying bytes.

complexityQuestion.prompt: For the fixed method “Group exact payload copies — analyzed method”, n is the number of payloads and B their total byte count. Override the fixed-size-key cost with the explicit byte-string dictionary model from the task: expected O(|s|+1) per operation, including hashing and exact equality. The dictionary retains input references; it uses constant auxiliary state for one comparison. Index appends have amortized constant cost. Choose its time and auxiliary-space pair. Use the tightest standard bound for the worst legal input for the stated size parameters, with expected time over non-adversarial hashing. Fixed-width integer and fixed-size tuple hash operations take expected amortized O(1); arithmetic, comparison and copying one integer take O(1). Auxiliary space excludes the supplied input and returned result, includes all maps, sets, temporary copies and call stacks. The method is iterative, with constant call-stack space.

feedback.reason: Include byte hashing/equality work while retaining references and bucket indices.
details: Distinguish a hash used for lookup from an exact key equality test required for correctness.
Summing expected O(|s|+1) dictionary costs over input payloads gives O(B+n). Appending and copying n indices adds O(n), for expected O(B+n+1).

At most n key references and dictionary records, plus n retained bucket indices, require O(n+1). Supplied bytes and returned group copies are excluded. Dictionary keys are references with equality support, not copied strings.
“Expected O(B + n + 1) time; O(n + 1) auxiliary space.”: Correct under the stated expected/amortized hashing model.
“Expected O(n + 1) time independent of B; O(n + 1) space.”: Hashing and equality read payload bytes under the explicit dictionary cost model.

“Expected O(B + n + 1) time; O(B+n+1) auxiliary space as the tight bound.”: The fixed method retains references into immutable input, not copied payload bytes; bucket indices and references cost O(n+1).

“Guaranteed O(B + n + 1) time for adversarial collisions; O(n + 1) space.”: The model is expected under non-adversarial hashing; correctness survives collisions but the time guarantee does not become unconditional.
